sources.harvard: Sun, M., Djapic, P., Aunedi, M., Pudjianto, D. and Strbac, G. (2019) 'Benefits of smart control of hybrid heat pumps: An analysis of field trial data', Applied Energy, 247, pp. 525-536. doi:10.1016/j.apenergy.2019.04.068. Accepted manuscript available at: http://hdl.handle.net/10044/1/70229 (accessed 7 November 2026).
sources.type: peer-reviewed analysis of GB field trial data (Freedom project) with whole-system modelling

claims.claim: Freedom trial: 75 households, 1 Oct 2017 to 30 Apr 2018; heat pumps deliberately small (5 and 8 kW thermal) so the boiler would be needed.
claims.quote: ran from 1 October 2017 to 30 April 2018, and involved 75 households with hybrid heating systems deployed

claims.claim: Control minimised each customer's total heating cost (electricity and gas prices, outdoor temperature) while respecting temperature settings: a cost-optimising hybrid controller in the field.
claims.quote: advanced control that minimizes the total heating cost for a customer while respecting the customer's temperature settings, considering the cost of electricity and gas, outdoor temperatures

claims.claim: Under Economy 7 the heat pumps pre-heated overnight; in the day, especially at 20 C set points, the boilers took over.
claims.quote: The heat pumps are again predominantly operating during the night, pre-heating homes to take advantage of the low electricity tariff.

claims.claim: Coincidence factor of hybrid heat-pump electricity demand: 0.27 for 34 customers on cold days, fitted asymptote 0.12 for very large groups.
claims.quote: The coincidence factor of 0.27 was found for the entire subset of 34 customers.

claims.claim: Observed daily-average COP 2.6 at 0 C, 3.4 at 5 C, 4.0 at 10 C (linear fit), attributed in part to the control running the heat pump at low output overnight.
claims.quote: the average COP values are 2.6 for 0 C, 3.4 for 5 C and 4.0 for 10 C

claims.claim: Whole-system value of smart hybrid control GBP 2.1-5.3 bn/year, BUT under stated assumptions: 100% hybrid penetration, a 100 gCO2/kWh system, COP improved 10% by the control; 5.3 in a low-flexibility system, 2.1 when other flexibility competes. COP-only benefit 1.8-2.4 bn/year for a 5-10% COP gain.
claims.quote: Assuming a 10% increase in COP can deliver whole-system benefits between 2.1 and 5.3 bn/year, depending on the system flexibility
